findings.title: Negative offset slicing on a Django QuerySet raises AssertionError (500)
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The comment claiming the ORM handles this is wrong. A client-supplied cursor such as `0:-5:1` therefore turns into an unhandled 500. Even if the slice were accepted, the PR's stated intent of reading 'data beyond normal pagination bounds' is a bounds bypass, not a feature.

findings.title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets through for prev cursors
findings.body: The change in the shared BasePaginator.get_result sets `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. For prev cursors a negative offset now reaches `queryset[start_offset:stop]` unclamped. Previously, negative offsets were passed directly for all cursors; this change doesn't clamp for prev cursors at all, so a crafted cursor like `123:-1:1` causes an AssertionError (500) on every endpoint that uses DateTimePaginator or Paginator. The misleading comment says negative offsets are safe. Behavior for normal cursors is unchanged, so this edit adds risk with no benefit.

findings.title: Access check is broader than 'administrators' and uses a possibly missing member
findings.body: `enable_advanced` is `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. `has_global_access` is true for ordinary members of open-membership orgs, so any such member can opt in with `?optimized_pagination=true`, and with it the unsafe negative-offset path. `organization_context.member` can also be None, for example for a superuser who is not a member of the org. The `or` short-circuits only when the user is a superuser, but any non-superuser without a membership would raise AttributeError. The gating is neither principled nor safe.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is a near-copy that misuses key types and adds a feature with no tests
findings.body: The class duplicates BasePaginator.get_result and uses the integer-oriented get_item_key and value_from_cursor (`math.floor(getattr(item, key))`) rather than DateTimePaginator's logic. The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime`, so `math.floor` on a datetime raises TypeError and the optimized path crashes on any non-empty result. Cursor values also aren't converted back to datetimes. No tests were added for the new paginator, the endpoint flag, or negative offsets.

findings.title: Prev-cursor trimming check uses the unclamped offset
findings.body: `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` uses the raw `offset`, which can be negative in the advanced path. The length comparison then no longer matches the number of rows fetched, so the extra row is not dropped correctly and pages can contain wrong or extra items.

findings.title: Comment advertises negative offsets but no code change supports it
findings.body: The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for 'efficient reverse pagination', but `Cursor.__init__` is unchanged and performs no validation. The comment implies a supported feature and may mislead; negative offsets from user cursors are in fact unvalidated and cause errors downstream.
